paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the beasts do NOT get the last word. Daniel sees four of them rise out of a churning sea, and they devour, crush and trample. But the one explaining the vision says the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and he says "forever and ever" (Daniel 7:18). I'm telling you, the loudest thing in the room is not always the one that wins.

Now look at what keeps the horn in check. It prevails against the saints "until the Ancient of Days arrived and pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High" (Daniel 7:21-22). The court convenes, the books are opened, and the dominion of the one who spoke against the Most High is "taken away and completely destroyed forever" (Daniel 7:26). Then One like the Son of Man is given a kingdom "that will never be destroyed" (Daniel 7:13-14). That's the Lamb's kingdom, friend, and it's why my ovens stay ready.

And Daniel? He's grieved, his face turns pale, and he keeps the matter to himself (Daniel 7:15, 28). I love him for that, because I think it shows an honest man taking the weight of what he saw. So if hard days feel like they're running the show, baker, remember that the Most High is the One who sets the ending. You can be shaken and still hold on, because the kingdom is His.
